# Claudopus

> Claudopus is a free, open-source (MIT) mod for Claude Code, Anthropic's coding agent, for macOS, Windows and Linux. Each message you send in a chat becomes a task that Claude runs in the background, so the chat is free for your next message straight away. A panel beside the chat shows every task as a card, questions that need you come to the top of it, and what each finished task found is kept in a Results list. Claudopus is not made by Anthropic.

- Website: https://www.claudopus.ai
- Source code: https://github.com/dimka3553/claudopus
- Latest release: https://github.com/dimka3553/claudopus/releases/latest
- Licence: MIT

## Install

In Terminal, on a Mac or Linux, one line:

```
curl -fsSL https://www.claudopus.ai/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell, one line:

```
irm https://www.claudopus.ai/install.ps1 | iex
```

It finds Claude Code (the Claude desktop app's own copy, or `claude` in a terminal), installs Claudopus from GitHub (dimka3553/claudopus) and switches it on, keeping the rest of `~/.claude/settings.json`. On a Mac without Apple's command line tools, it opens their installer and carries on once they are in; on Windows without Git for Windows or jq, it installs them with winget first. Then open a new chat in the desktop app's Code tab, or type `/reload-plugins` in one that is open; `/claudopus` opens the panel.

At the prompt of Claude Code in a terminal, the same in two lines:

```
/plugin marketplace add dimka3553/claudopus
/plugin install claudopus@claudopus
```

## What it does

- One chat runs many tasks at once: each request is its own background task, and the chat stays small because the work happens in the tasks.
- The panel shows each task's to-dos, how far it has got, its helpers and its long commands; Stop ends a task.
- Questions, permission prompts and releases from every chat wait at the top of the panel with answer buttons, a sound and a notification.
- Results keeps what each finished task found, with its pictures, as plain files on your machine.
- Memory keeps your messages word for word and notes on each topic, so later chats can look them up.
- Each task changes code in a worktree and branch of its own, and reaches main only after you press Release it.
- A second agent that did not do the work can check it before you see it, when you ask for one or turn it on in Config.
- Tasks that run side by side use tokens side by side: five at once use them about five times as fast as one.

## Figures from real use

The author's own use (29 Oct to 21 Nov 2026), from Claudopus's Stats tab: about three weeks of work done in one week, which is 19 days 14 hours of task time in 6 days 13 hours of real time, so about three tasks ran whenever any ran. 825 tasks were done, up to 18 at once. That is not three times the output, and it is not cheaper: it used 20.44 billion tokens.
